info.name: Open-S3 API
info.description:
Self-hosted S3-compatible storage API (CodeIgniter), single fixed Access Key/Secret Key account, multi-bucket. Implements the 3 upload usecases from docs/AWS_S3_Integration_Best_Practices.md:

1. **Presigned URL** direct upload/download (`Presigned URL` folder)
2. **Backend upload** with a server-side pipeline — validate, virus scan, thumbnail (`Backend Upload` folder)
3. **Hybrid/event** — every object write/delete queues an event the worker processes async (see `Events (debug)` folder)

### Authentication
Every endpoint except `GET /healthz` requires a signed request. Two **independent** signing schemes are accepted — the server auto-detects which one a request is using:

1. **`OS3-HMAC-SHA256`** — this project's own scheme (see `application/libraries/Sigv4_signer.php`). This is what this collection uses, via a collection-level pre-request script that signs every request automatically — set `access_key_id` / `secret_access_key` in the collection variables (values come from your `open-s3/.env`) and everything else just works.
2. **`AWS4-HMAC-SHA256`** — the real AWS SigV4 spec (see `application/libraries/Aws_sigv4_signer.php`), so an unmodified AWS SDK (`@aws-sdk/client-s3`, `boto3`, `aws-cli`, MinIO client...) works by just pointing `endpoint` at this server with the same Access Key/Secret Key — no need to call `/internal/presign` at all; the SDK's own presigner (`getSignedUrl`) produces a URL this server verifies natively. **This collection does not exercise that path** (it always sends `OS3-HMAC-SHA256`); use a real AWS SDK client for that instead.

Two auth modes for `OS3-HMAC-SHA256`, both implemented by this collection's pre-request script:
- **Header auth** (used by every request here): `Authorization: OS3-HMAC-SHA256 Credential=<access_key_id>, SignedHeaders=host;x-os3-date, Signature=<hex>` + `X-Os3-Date` header.
- **Query-string auth** (presigned URLs): `X-Os3-Credential`, `X-Os3-Date`, `X-Os3-Expires`, `X-Os3-SignedHeaders`, `X-Os3-Signature` query params — generated by the `Generate Presigned URL` requests below; paste the returned `url` into a browser/curl/new request, no extra headers needed.

### CORS
Calling the API straight from a browser on another origin (typical for the presigned-URL usecase) needs `cors_config` set on the bucket first — with none set, no `Access-Control-*` headers are sent at all (same secure-by-default behavior as real S3), so the browser blocks the call. See `Bucket Policy → Update Bucket Policy` for the config shape and `Bucket Policy → CORS Preflight (OPTIONS)` for a worked example.

### Variables
- `base_url` — e.g. `http://localhost:8080` (must match `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` in `.env` for presigned URLs to verify correctly)
- `access_key_id` / `secret_access_key` — from `.env`
- `bucket` / `key` — scratch values used across the example requests

### Running it
```
cd open-s3 && docker compose up -d --build
```
then either run the whole collection top-to-bottom (folders are ordered so `Create Bucket` runs before anything that needs `{{bucket}}`, and `Cleanup` runs last), or open individual requests to explore the API — `Backend Upload` needs a real file attached manually in Postman's UI (its form-data field has no file preset, since collections can't embed one).

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness/readiness check. No authentication required — used by docker-compose healthchecks.

request.description: Returns `{"status":"ok"}` with HTTP 200 if the app can serve requests. Does not touch the database.
`GET /` — lists every bucket on the account. Returns `ListAllMyBucketsResult` XML.

`PUT /{bucket}` — creates a bucket. Idempotent: creating a bucket you already own returns 200 (single-account semantics — no `BucketAlreadyExists` conflict). Bucket names must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9\-.]{1,61}[a-z0-9]$` or you get `400 InvalidBucketName`.

`GET /{bucket}` — lists objects (current versions only). Returns `ListBucketResult` XML.

Query params: `prefix` (filter), `marker` (pagination cursor — last key from the previous page), `max-keys` (default/clamp 1000).

item.name: Objects
item.description: S3-compatible object operations. Every PUT/DELETE here also queues an `object.created` / `object.removed` event for the worker (see `Events (debug)`).

request.description:
`PUT /{bucket}/{key}` — uploads the request body as the object. Set `Content-Type` to whatever the object actually is (drives thumbnailing downstream if it's an image). Response `ETag` header is the object's MD5.

Custom metadata: send headers like `X-Os3-Meta-Foo: bar` — stored and retrievable, not currently echoed back on GET/HEAD.

body.raw: Hello from the Open-S3 Postman collection!

request.description: `GET /{bucket}/{key}` — downloads the object body. 404 `NoSuchKey` if missing.
Same as Get Object but with a `Range` header — returns `206 Partial Content` with `Content-Range: bytes start-end/total`, or `416` if the range is invalid.
`HEAD /{bucket}/{key}` — metadata only (ETag, Content-Type, Content-Length, Last-Modified), no body. 404 `NoSuchKey` if missing.

`DELETE /{bucket}/{key}` — deletes the object (204). If the bucket has versioning enabled and no `versionId` query param is given, this inserts a delete-marker instead of removing prior versions; pass `?versionId=...` to hard-delete a specific version.

**Not implemented yet** (see docs/plans.md Phase 7 — roadmap). Any request with a `uploads` or `uploadId` query param currently returns `501 NotImplemented`. Included here so the gap is documented, not hidden.

item.name: Presigned URL (usecase 1)
item.description: Direct-upload/download usecase: your backend calls `/internal/presign` (signed like everything else in this collection) to get a short-lived URL; the browser/mobile client then hits that URL directly — no Access Key ever reaches the client.

request.description: Returns a presigned `PUT` URL valid for `expiresIn` seconds (clamped to 60–900s). Copy the `url` field from the response into a new request (method PUT, raw body = file contents) to upload directly — no Authorization header needed, the URL itself carries the signature.
Same as above but for downloads — returns a presigned `GET` URL so a client can fetch a private object without any credentials.

item.name: Backend Upload (usecase 2)
item.description: Server-mediated upload usecase: your backend streams the file through Open-S3 itself, which runs a pipeline before storing it — size/mime validation, virus scan (if `ENABLE_VIRUS_SCAN=true`), and (for images) an automatic `<key>.thumb.jpg` thumbnail.

request.description: Field name must be `file`. On success returns JSON with `etag`/`size`; for image Content-Types, a sibling `{key}.thumb.jpg` object is created automatically (check `Objects → List Objects` afterwards). Rejects with `400 VirusDetected` if ClamAV flags the file (only when antivirus is enabled).

item.name: Bucket Policy
item.description: Per-bucket configuration — not part of the S3 REST API, a convenience endpoint.

request.description: Merges any subset of these fields onto the bucket (unspecified fields are left unchanged): `versioning_enabled`, `is_public`, `cors_config` (object, see below), `notification_url` (webhook target for usecase 3), `max_object_size` (bytes), `allowed_mime_types` (array — omit/null to allow any type). **`cors_config`** — like real S3, a bucket with no `cors_config` sends *no* `Access-Control-*` headers at all, so cross-origin browser calls (e.g. a presigned PUT from a web app on another domain) are blocked. Set it to enable CORS: `allowed_origins` (array, `"*"` matches any), `allowed_methods`, `allowed_headers`, `expose_headers` (headers JS can read via `response.headers.get(...)`, e.g. `ETag`), `max_age` (seconds the browser caches the preflight). Applies to every bucket/object request in the `Buckets`/`Objects` folders (and presigned URLs), including auto-answering the `OPTIONS` preflight with no auth required. **`is_public`** — default `false`. When `true`, `GET`/`HEAD` on an *object* in this bucket needs no signature at all (e.g. a plain `` or an unsigned `fetch`) — scoped narrowly: bucket-level listing (`GET /{bucket}`) and every write (`PUT`/`DELETE`) still always require a valid signature, even on a public bucket. Combine with `cors_config` if browser JS needs to read the response cross-origin, not just display it in an `` tag.

Simulates a browser's CORS preflight for a cross-origin `PUT` (e.g. before a presigned upload from a web app). Run this AFTER `Update Bucket Policy` above, which sets `cors_config.allowed_origins` to include `https://example.com` — a bucket with no `cors_config` instead falls through to normal auth and returns `403` (no CORS headers at all), same as an unconfigured bucket on real S3.

On success: `204` with no auth required, plus `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`, `Access-Control-Max-Age`. The same `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header is also added to the *actual* GET/PUT/etc. response afterwards (see `application/core/MY_Controller.php::apply_cors`), not just this preflight — required for the browser to let JS read the response.

Demonstrates `is_public` (set to `true` by `Update Bucket Policy` above): object `GET`/`HEAD` needs no signature at all once a bucket is public. This collection's pre-request script still attaches an `Authorization` header to every request including this one — harmless (the server skips auth entirely for a public-bucket object read, it doesn't just tolerate a valid-but-unnecessary one) — but it means running this from here doesn't *prove* anonymity. To actually verify: `curl -i {{base_url}}/{{bucket}}/{{key}}` with no headers at all, or load it in a plain ``/incognito tab. In a full top-to-bottom collection run `{{key}}` (`hello.txt`) was already deleted back in the `Objects` folder, so expect `404 NoSuchKey` here rather than the object body — that 404 (instead of `403 AccessDenied`) is itself the proof auth was skipped; re-run `Objects → Put Object` first to see an actual `200` with content.

item.name: Events (debug)
item.description: Hybrid/event usecase (usecase 3): every object PUT/DELETE (from any of the folders above) inserts a row here and pushes it to the Redis queue; the `worker` container consumes it (thumbnailing, async virus scan, webhook to the bucket's `notification_url`). This endpoint is for observing that pipeline, not part of the S3 API surface.

request.description: Optional `status` query param: `pending` | `processing` | `done` | `failed`. Returns the 100 most recent events, newest first.

item.name: Cleanup
item.description: Run last, not as part of the `Buckets` folder — `{{bucket}}` is still needed by every folder above (Objects, Presigned URL, Backend Upload, Bucket Policy). Deletes the demo bucket created by `Buckets → Create Bucket`.

request.description: `DELETE /{bucket}` — deletes an empty bucket (204). Returns `409 BucketNotEmpty` if it still has objects — e.g. if `Backend Upload` actually stored a file (with its auto-generated thumbnail) earlier in the run; delete those objects first with `Objects → Delete Object` (adjusting `{{key}}`).
